name: Nile
fact: Traditionally ranked the longest river in the world at about 6,650 km, flowing north into the Mediterranean.

name: Amazon River
fact: Carries more water than any other river on Earth, roughly a fifth of all river discharge into the oceans.

name: Yangtze
fact: The longest river in Asia and home to the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station by capacity.

name: Mississippi River
fact: Its drainage basin covers all or part of 32 US states and two Canadian provinces.

name: Yenisei
fact: Often treated as the dividing line between Western and Eastern Siberia; it flows north into the Kara Sea.

name: Yellow River
fact: Named for the huge loads of yellowish loess silt it carries; called both the cradle of Chinese civilization and China's Sorrow.

name: Ob River
fact: Its estuary, the Gulf of Ob, is one of the longest estuaries in the world at around 1,000 km.

name: Congo River
where: DR Congo, Republic of the Congo
fact: The deepest river in the world, with measured depths over 220 m, and it crosses the equator twice.

name: Mekong
where: China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam
fact: Flows through six countries and ends in a vast delta in southern Vietnam known as the Nine Dragons.

name: Danube
fact: Flows through ten countries, more than any other river, and passes four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.

name: Volga
fact: The longest river in Europe; it drains into the Caspian Sea, which has no outlet to the ocean.

name: Rhine
fact: Rises in the Swiss Alps and reaches the North Sea at Rotterdam, Europe's busiest port.

name: Ganges
fact: Sacred in Hinduism; together with the Brahmaputra it forms the world's largest delta, the Sundarbans region.

name: Indus River
fact: Gave its name to India and the Indus Valley Civilisation; most of its length is in Pakistan.

name: Euphrates
fact: With the Tigris it bounds Mesopotamia, 'the land between the rivers'; they merge as the Shatt al-Arab.

name: Tigris
fact: Baghdad was built on its banks; the ancient city of Nineveh sat across from modern Mosul.

name: Niger River
fact: Takes a strange boomerang route, first flowing away from the sea toward the Sahara near Timbuktu before turning south.

name: Zambezi
fact: Plunges over Victoria Falls and feeds two giant reservoirs, Lake Kariba and Cahora Bassa.

name: Orinoco
fact: Linked to the Amazon basin by the Casiquiare canal, a natural river that splits and flows into two systems.

name: Paraná River
fact: Joins the Uruguay River to form the Río de la Plata; the Itaipu Dam sits on it at the Brazil and Paraguay border.

name: Murray River
fact: Australia's longest river; for much of its length it forms the border between New South Wales and Victoria.

name: Colorado River
fact: Carved the Grand Canyon; so much of it is diverted that it often fails to reach the Gulf of California.

name: Saint Lawrence River
fact: Drains the Great Lakes to the Atlantic, passing Montreal and Quebec City.

name: Mackenzie River
fact: Canada's longest river system, flowing north through the Northwest Territories into the Beaufort Sea.

name: River Thames
fact: Flows through Oxford and London; the stretch through Oxford is traditionally called the Isis.

name: Seine
fact: The riverbanks through central Paris are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Jordan River
fact: Flows from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea, ending at the lowest land point on Earth.

name: Brahmaputra
fact: Called the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, where it cuts one of the deepest canyons on Earth.

name: Lena
fact: Its delta in the Laptev Sea is one of the largest in the world and freezes for most of the year.

name: Amur River
fact: Forms a long stretch of the border between Russia and China, where it is called the Heilong Jiang, Black Dragon River.

name: Mount Everest
fact: Highest point above sea level at 8,849 m; Nepalis call it Sagarmatha and Tibetans Chomolungma.

name: K2
fact: The second highest mountain, nicknamed the Savage Mountain for its high fatality rate; first climbed in winter only in 2021.

name: Kangchenjunga
fact: The third highest mountain and the highest point in India.

name: Aconcagua
fact: At 6,961 m it is the highest mountain outside Asia and the highest in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres.

name: Denali
fact: North America's highest peak; its base to peak rise of about 5,500 m is larger than Everest's.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
fact: Africa's highest peak and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world, a dormant volcano with shrinking glaciers.

name: Mount Elbrus
fact: A dormant volcano in the Caucasus, often counted as Europe's highest peak at 5,642 m.

name: Mont Blanc
fact: Highest peak in the Alps; France and Italy still disagree over exactly where the border runs on the summit.

name: Vinson Massif
fact: Antarctica's highest mountain, one of the Seven Summits, first climbed in 1966.

name: Puncak Jaya
fact: Highest island peak in the world and the highest point in Oceania, near the huge Grasberg mine.

name: Chimborazo
fact: Thanks to Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the farthest point from Earth's center.

name: Mount Fuji
fact: Japan's highest peak at 3,776 m, an active stratovolcano that last erupted in 1707.

name: Matterhorn
fact: Its near-perfect pyramid shape makes it one of the most photographed mountains; first climbed in 1865.

name: Mount Olympus
fact: Highest mountain in Greece and mythical home of the twelve Olympian gods.

name: Mount Ararat
fact: Sits in Turkey but is a national symbol of Armenia and appears on its coat of arms.

name: Mount Damavand
fact: The highest volcano in Asia and the highest peak in the Middle East.

name: Mount Etna
fact: One of the most active volcanoes on Earth and the tallest active volcano in Europe.

name: Mount Vesuvius
fact: Buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 79; around three million people live near it today.

name: Krakatoa
fact: Its 1883 eruption was heard nearly 5,000 km away, possibly the loudest sound in recorded history.

name: Mount Tambora
fact: Its 1815 eruption caused 1816's 'Year Without a Summer' across Europe and North America.

name: Mauna Kea
fact: Measured from its base on the sea floor it is over 10,000 m tall, taller than Everest.

name: Eyjafjallajökull
fact: Its 2010 eruption grounded most European air traffic for about a week.

name: Ojos del Salado
fact: The highest active volcano in the world at 6,893 m.

name: Himalayas
fact: Contains 10 of the 14 peaks over 8,000 m, including Everest; the name means 'abode of snow' in Sanskrit.

name: Andes
fact: The longest continental mountain range, about 7,000 km, running through seven countries.

name: Alps
where: France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria and more
fact: Stretch across eight countries in an arc about 1,200 km long.

name: Rocky Mountains
fact: Their highest peak is Mount Elbert in Colorado at 4,401 m.

name: Ural Mountains
fact: Form the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.

name: Atlas Mountains
fact: Separate the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara; highest point Toubkal at 4,167 m.

name: Appalachian Mountains
fact: Among the oldest mountains on Earth, once as tall as the Alps; highest point Mount Mitchell in North Carolina.

name: Carpathian Mountains
where: Romania, Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine and more
fact: Europe's second longest range, curving in an arc through Central and Eastern Europe, home to large brown bear populations.

name: Pyrenees
fact: Form the natural border between France and Spain, with Andorra nestled inside.

name: Caucasus Mountains
fact: One of the most linguistically diverse regions on Earth, with dozens of languages.

name: Karakoram
fact: Has the highest concentration of peaks over 8,000 m, including K2, and huge glaciers like Siachen.

name: Tian Shan
fact: The name means 'Heavenly Mountains' in Chinese; about 80 percent of Kyrgyzstan is mountainous.

name: Great Dividing Range
fact: Australia's longest range, running over 3,500 km down the east coast.

name: Drakensberg
fact: Means 'dragon mountains' in Afrikaans; famous for San rock art.

name: Sahara
fact: The largest hot desert, about the size of the United States; only a small part is sand dunes.

name: Gobi Desert
fact: A cold desert where dinosaur eggs were first found by scientists in the 1920s.

name: Atacama Desert
fact: The driest non-polar desert; some weather stations have never recorded rain.

name: Kalahari Desert
fact: Technically a semi-desert since it gets enough rain to support grasses and wildlife.

name: Namib
fact: Considered the oldest desert in the world, with some of the tallest sand dunes at Sossusvlei.

name: Rub' al Khali
fact: The Empty Quarter is the largest continuous sand desert on Earth.

name: Taklamakan Desert
fact: The Silk Road split to skirt its northern and southern edges rather than cross it.

name: Thar Desert
fact: One of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

name: Mojave Desert
fact: Contains Death Valley, where the highest air temperature on Earth, 56.7 C, was recorded.

name: Patagonian Desert
fact: The largest desert in the Americas, a cold rain shadow desert behind the Andes.

name: Danakil Desert
fact: One of the hottest places on Earth by year-round average temperature, sitting largely below sea level.

name: Caspian Sea
fact: The largest lake on Earth by area; whether it is legally a sea or lake affected how five countries split its oil.

name: Lake Superior
fact: The largest freshwater lake by surface area; it holds enough water to cover North and South America 30 cm deep.

name: Lake Baikal
fact: The deepest and oldest lake in the world, holding about 20 percent of Earth's unfrozen fresh surface water.

name: Lake Victoria
fact: Africa's largest lake and the main source of the White Nile.

name: Lake Tanganyika
fact: The longest freshwater lake in the world and the second deepest after Baikal.

name: Lake Malawi
fact: Has more fish species than any other lake, most of them colorful cichlids found nowhere else.

name: Lake Titicaca
fact: Often called the highest navigable lake in the world at 3,812 m; the Uros people live on floating reed islands.

name: Dead Sea
fact: Its shore is the lowest land on Earth, over 430 m below sea level, and its water is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean.

name: Aral Sea
fact: Once the fourth largest lake, it largely dried up after Soviet irrigation projects diverted its rivers.

name: Lake Chad
fact: Shrank by about 90 percent after the 1960s, though it has partly stabilized.

name: Tonlé Sap
fact: Its river reverses direction each monsoon, making the lake swell to several times its dry season size.

name: Lake Ladoga
fact: Europe's largest lake; its frozen surface was the 'Road of Life' supplying besieged Leningrad.

name: Great Salt Lake
fact: The largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere; its level rises and falls dramatically.

name: Crater Lake
fact: The deepest lake in the US, filling the caldera of the collapsed volcano Mount Mazama.

name: Lake Geneva
fact: Called Lac Léman in French; one of Western Europe's largest lakes.

name: Issyk-Kul
fact: A salty mountain lake that never freezes despite its altitude; the name means 'warm lake'.

name: Victoria Falls
fact: Locally called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'; the largest sheet of falling water.

name: Angel Falls
fact: The world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 m, falling off a flat-topped tepui.

name: Iguazu Falls
fact: About 275 separate falls; the biggest is called the Devil's Throat.

name: Niagara Falls
fact: Three falls on the border; the Horseshoe Falls is mostly in Canada.

name: Kaieteur Falls
fact: One of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls, about four times taller than Niagara.

name: Gullfoss
fact: The 'Golden Falls', part of Iceland's popular Golden Circle route.

name: Greenland
fact: The world's largest island; about 80 percent is covered by an ice sheet up to 3 km thick.

name: New Guinea
fact: The second largest island, with over 800 languages spoken on it.

name: Borneo
fact: The only island shared by three countries.

name: Madagascar
fact: About 90 percent of its wildlife is found nowhere else, including all lemurs.

name: Baffin Island
fact: The fifth largest island in the world, part of Nunavut.

name: Sumatra
fact: The equator crosses it; home to the Sumatran tiger and orangutan.

name: Honshu
fact: The seventh largest island and the second most populous island after Java.

name: Java
fact: The most populous island on Earth, with over 150 million people.

name: Great Britain
fact: The largest island in Europe and the ninth largest in the world.

name: Tasmania
fact: Separated from mainland Australia by the Bass Strait; about 40 percent is protected land.

name: Socotra
fact: Its dragon's blood trees and other plants are so unusual it's been called the most alien place on Earth.

name: Galápagos Islands
fact: Their finches and tortoises helped inspire Darwin's theory of natural selection.

name: Svalbard
fact: Home to the Global Seed Vault; polar bears outnumber the roughly 3,000 residents.

name: Faroe Islands
fact: More sheep than people; the name is thought to mean 'sheep islands'.

name: Azores
fact: Nine volcanic islands sitting on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where three tectonic plates meet.

name: Canary Islands
fact: Named after dogs (Latin canis), not birds; Teide on Tenerife is Spain's highest peak.

name: Maldives
fact: The lowest country on Earth, averaging about 1.5 m above sea level.

name: Strait of Gibraltar
fact: Connects the Atlantic and Mediterranean; only about 13 km wide at its narrowest.

name: Strait of Hormuz
fact: About a fifth of the world's oil passes through this chokepoint.

name: Strait of Malacca
fact: One of the world's busiest shipping lanes, linking the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

name: Bosphorus
fact: Splits Istanbul between Europe and Asia, making it a city on two continents.

name: Bering Strait
fact: The Diomede Islands in the middle are 4 km apart but on opposite sides of the International Date Line.

name: Strait of Magellan
fact: Sailed by Magellan in 1520; it separates mainland South America from Tierra del Fuego.

name: Drake Passage
fact: Between Cape Horn and Antarctica; famous for some of the roughest seas on the planet.

name: Strait of Dover
fact: The narrowest part of the English Channel at about 33 km, crossed by the Channel Tunnel beneath.

name: Bab-el-Mandeb
fact: The name means 'Gate of Grief'; it links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

name: Suez Canal
fact: Opened in 1869, it lets ships skip sailing around Africa; the Ever Given blocked it for six days in 2021.

name: Panama Canal
fact: Uses locks to lift ships 26 m to Gatun Lake; ships heading to the Pacific actually travel southeast.

name: Grand Canyon
fact: Up to 1,800 m deep, exposing nearly two billion years of rock layers.

name: Fish River Canyon
fact: The largest canyon in Africa.

name: Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon
fact: Considered the deepest canyon on Earth, over 5,000 m in places.

name: Tibetan Plateau
fact: The 'Roof of the World', averaging over 4,500 m; its glaciers feed rivers for nearly two billion people.

name: Altiplano
fact: The largest high plateau outside Tibet, holding Lake Titicaca and the Uyuni salt flat.

name: Salar de Uyuni
fact: The world's largest salt flat, so flat that satellites use it for calibration; turns into a giant mirror after rain.

name: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The largest structure built by living things, stretching over 2,300 km.

name: Great Blue Hole
fact: A 300 m wide marine sinkhole made famous by Jacques Cousteau.

name: Uluru
fact: A sacred sandstone monolith that seems to change color at sunrise and sunset; climbing was banned in 2019.

name: Giant's Causeway
fact: About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns from an ancient lava flow.

name: Ha Long Bay
fact: Thousands of limestone karst islands; the name means 'descending dragon'.

name: Bay of Fundy
fact: Has the highest tides in the world, up to 16 m.

name: Bay of Bengal
fact: The largest bay in the world.

name: Hudson Bay
fact: A huge inland sea; the land around it is still rising after the weight of Ice Age glaciers lifted.

name: Mediterranean Sea
fact: Nearly dried out about 6 million years ago in the Messinian salinity crisis.

name: Sargasso Sea
fact: The only sea with no land coastline, bounded only by ocean currents.

name: Black Sea
where: Turkey, Ukraine, Russia, Romania, Bulgaria, Georgia
fact: Its deep waters have almost no oxygen, preserving ancient shipwrecks remarkably well.

name: Red Sea
where: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Sudan and more
fact: One of the saltiest seas; no rivers flow into it.

name: Baltic Sea
fact: Brackish, with low salinity, because many rivers feed it and it is nearly enclosed.

name: South China Sea
where: China, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia and more
fact: Contains the disputed Spratly and Paracel Islands.

name: Mariana Trench
fact: Its Challenger Deep is about 10,900 m, the deepest known point in the oceans.

name: Iberian Peninsula
fact: Includes the southwesternmost point of mainland Europe, Cabo de São Vicente.

name: Arabian Peninsula
fact: The largest peninsula in the world.

name: Kamchatka Peninsula
fact: Has around 160 volcanoes, about 29 of them active, and the Valley of Geysers.

name: Yucatán Peninsula
fact: Nearly riverless; water flows underground through thousands of sinkholes called cenotes, near the Chicxulub crater.

name: Horn of Africa
fact: The easternmost projection of the African continent.

name: Cape Horn
fact: Sailors who rounded it traditionally earned the right to wear a gold earring.

name: Cape of Good Hope
fact: Not Africa's southernmost point; that is Cape Agulhas, about 150 km away.

name: North Cape
fact: Often billed as Europe's northernmost point, though a nearby spit called Knivskjellodden goes slightly farther.

name: Serengeti
fact: Hosts the Great Migration of over a million wildebeest each year.

name: Pampas
fact: Fertile lowlands and home of the gaucho, Argentina's cowboy.

name: Eurasian Steppe
fact: A grassland highway across Eurasia used by Scythians, Huns and Mongols.

name: Okavango Delta
fact: An inland delta where a river floods into the Kalahari and evaporates without reaching the sea.

name: Pantanal
fact: The world's largest tropical wetland and one of the best places to see jaguars.

name: Sundarbans
fact: The largest mangrove forest, home to Bengal tigers that swim between islands.

name: Amazon rainforest
where: Brazil and eight other countries or territories
fact: The largest tropical rainforest, spanning nine countries and territories.

name: Daintree Rainforest
fact: Believed to be one of the oldest continuously surviving tropical rainforests, around 180 million years old.

name: Black Forest
fact: Birthplace of the cuckoo clock and the source of the Danube.

name: Great Rift Valley
fact: Africa is slowly splitting apart here; one day the east may become a separate landmass.

name: Þingvellir
fact: You can snorkel between the North American and Eurasian plates in the Silfra fissure; also site of one of the oldest parliaments.

name: Cappadocia
fact: Known for fairy chimney rock spires and whole underground cities carved into soft volcanic rock.

name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
fact: Towering sandstone pillars that helped inspire the floating mountains in the film Avatar.

name: Pamukkale
fact: White travertine terraces from hot springs; the name means 'cotton castle'.

name: Milford Sound
fact: Technically a fjord, not a sound; one of the wettest inhabited places on Earth.

name: Geirangerfjord
fact: A UNESCO site famous for the Seven Sisters waterfalls.

name: Sognefjord
fact: The longest and deepest fjord in Norway, reaching over 200 km inland.

name: Meteora
fact: Monasteries perched atop giant rock pillars; monks once reached them by rope baskets.

name: Vatnajökull
fact: Europe's largest glacier by volume, covering active volcanoes beneath.

name: Perito Moreno Glacier
fact: One of the few glaciers not retreating; it periodically dams a lake and then ruptures spectacularly.

name: Lambert Glacier
fact: The world's largest glacier, draining about 8 percent of the Antarctic ice sheet.

name: Yellowstone Caldera
fact: A supervolcano under the first national park in the world, home to half of Earth's geysers.

name: Lake Natron
fact: So alkaline it can calcify dead animals; still a key breeding ground for lesser flamingos.

name: Lake Hillier
fact: A bubblegum pink lake, colored by salt-loving algae and bacteria.

name: Dallol
fact: Acidic hot springs create yellow, green and orange mineral landscapes that look extraterrestrial.

name: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
fact: White sand dunes with blue rainwater lagoons between them every rainy season.

name: Chocolate Hills
fact: Over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season, like chocolate kisses.

name: Darvaza gas crater
fact: Nicknamed the Door to Hell, a natural gas crater that has been burning since around 1971.

name: Sossusvlei
fact: Rust red dunes over 300 m tall surround Deadvlei's ancient dead trees.

name: Table Mountain
fact: A flat-topped mountain over Cape Town, often draped in cloud called the 'tablecloth'.

name: Mount Roraima
fact: A tabletop mountain where three countries meet; it inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's The Lost World.

name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
fact: New Zealand's highest mountain; Edmund Hillary trained here before Everest.

name: Mount Kosciuszko
fact: Mainland Australia's highest point at just 2,228 m, named after a Polish hero.

name: Ben Nevis
fact: The highest mountain in the British Isles at 1,345 m.

name: Mount Sinai
fact: Traditionally where Moses received the Ten Commandments; Saint Catherine's Monastery sits at its foot.

name: Mount St. Helens
fact: Its 1980 eruption blew away the top 400 m of the mountain.

name: Popocatépetl
fact: One of the most active volcanoes in Mexico, visible from Mexico City; nicknamed El Popo.

name: Mount Pinatubo
fact: Its 1991 eruption cooled global temperatures by about 0.5 C for over a year.

name: Mount Nyiragongo
fact: Holds one of the world's largest lava lakes; its lava is unusually fast and runny.

name: Mount Erebus
fact: The southernmost active volcano, with a persistent lava lake.

name: Stromboli
fact: Erupts so often it's called the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean.

name: Camargue
fact: The Rhône delta, famous for white horses, black bulls and pink flamingos.

name: Lake Bled
fact: Has Slovenia's only natural island, topped by a church with a wishing bell.

name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
fact: Sixteen terraced lakes linked by waterfalls, with colors shifting from turquoise to green.

name: Lake Louise
fact: Its turquoise color comes from glacial rock flour suspended in the water.

name: Inle Lake
fact: Fishermen row with one leg wrapped around the oar.

name: Moeraki Boulders
fact: Nearly spherical boulders on a beach, formed like pearls in ancient seafloor mud.

name: Kerguelen Islands
fact: Nicknamed the Desolation Islands, among the most isolated places on Earth.

name: Tristan da Cunha
fact: The most remote inhabited archipelago, about 2,400 km from the nearest inhabited land.

name: Easter Island
fact: Home to nearly 1,000 moai statues; locals call it Rapa Nui.

name: Pitcairn Islands
fact: Settled by HMS Bounty mutineers; about 50 residents, one of the least populous jurisdictions on Earth.

name: Bouvet Island
fact: Often called the most remote island in the world; it's mostly covered by a glacier.

name: Point Nemo
fact: The farthest ocean point from land; astronauts on the ISS are often closer than the nearest humans on Earth.

name: Benagil Cave
fact: A sea cave on the Algarve coast with a hole in its dome that lets in a beam of sunlight.

name: Sơn Đoòng Cave
fact: The largest known cave passage in the world, with its own jungle and clouds inside.

name: Mammoth Cave National Park
fact: The longest known cave system in the world, with over 680 km surveyed.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
fact: Thousands of glowworms light the ceilings like a starry sky.

name: Death Valley
fact: Holds the record high air temperature and the lowest point in North America, Badwater Basin at 86 m below sea level.

name: Qattara Depression
fact: A huge low basin reaching 133 m below sea level; it anchored the El Alamein battle line in World War II.

name: Danube Delta
fact: Europe's best preserved delta and a paradise for pelicans.

name: Cliffs of Moher
fact: Rising about 214 m over the Atlantic; they appeared in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince.

name: White Cliffs of Dover
fact: Chalk cliffs made of tiny fossil plankton, visible from France on a clear day.

name: Nazca Lines
fact: Giant ancient desert drawings of animals and lines, best seen from the air.

name: Lofoten
fact: Arctic islands with an unusually mild climate thanks to the Gulf Stream.

name: Cabo da Roca
fact: The westernmost point of mainland Europe.

name: Tierra del Fuego
fact: 'Land of Fire', named for fires Magellan's crew saw burning on shore; Ushuaia claims to be the world's southernmost city.

name: Zanzibar
fact: The Spice Islands; its 1896 war with Britain is often called the shortest war in history.

name: Sicily
fact: The largest island in the Mediterranean.

name: Cyprus
fact: Has British military bases that are sovereign UK territory.

name: Sri Lanka
fact: Once called Ceylon; a chain of shoals called Adam's Bridge almost links it to India.

name: Kinabalu
fact: The highest peak on Borneo, home to carnivorous pitcher plants.
